purpose: Independent exact-reference mapping of the HBB promoter MPRA target; no score/outcome analysis or model fitting.

target.coordinate_interpretation: Metadata start/end match one-based inclusive genomic coordinates; internally represented as zero-based half-open.

region_partition.region: Upstream of annotated RefSeq transcription start; promoter-containing interval

clinical_overlap_example.note: Negative c. notation is relative to the coding start. It does not imply a base is upstream of the transcription start or a promoter-only variant.

independent_method: Fetch only score-set metadata and take its exact target DNA sequence; do not inspect score rows or score patterns.
Convert candidate metadata one-based inclusive coordinates to zero-based [start-1,end). Verify that interval length equals the 187-base target.
Compare both the forward genomic slice and its reverse complement with the entire target; additionally search both orientations across the 2,500-base verified reference bundle.
Intersect the resolved interval with explicit minus-strand transcript/CDS boundaries. Verify the 50-base transcribed portion equals the reverse complement of the first 50 bases of NM_000518.5.
Map the known c.-43C>T variant independently using genomic, target, and transcript position arithmetic, including complemented allele bases.
assumptions_and_limits: Exact sequence agreement resolves coordinate/strand interpretation for this frozen target; it does not establish genome-wide uniqueness beyond the 2,500-base bundle.

The target DNA is stored in plus genomic orientation while HBB transcription uses the minus strand. Physical reporter insertion/orientation must be read from the experimental methods, not inferred solely from target sequence.
The assay label HBB promoter names the full fragment; it includes 50 transcribed 5-prime UTR bases as well as 137 upstream bases. Neither all bases nor all variants can be called promoter-only.
Mapping does not attribute a reporter phenotype to transcription-factor binding, RNA stability, splicing, translation, endogenous gene regulation or clinical disease.
No outcome distribution, assay score, training pattern, prediction threshold or classifier was inspected to establish this mapping.
Metadata advertise a CC0 score-set license. This records the metadata and does not alter the paper, third-party annotation, or reference-data license scope.
